data.name: Fransisco
data.gender_notes: Fransisco is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Spanish name Francisco, which is derived from the Latin name Franciscus, meaning 'Frenchman' or 'free man'. The name gained popularity during the Middle Ages due to Saint Francis of Assisi, who was known for his devotion to poverty and nature. The name Fransisco carries the meaning “Frenchman, Free man” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Fransisco usually hope their child will grow to embody frenchman, free man and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of devotion, humility, and freedom

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fransisco total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: פרנסיסקו
in_hebrew.meaning: פרנסיסקו משמעותו האיש החופשי או הצרפתי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פרנסיסקו הוא שם שמקורו בלטינית, נגזר מהמילה 'פרנקיסקוס', שפירושה 'האיש החופשי' או 'הצרפתי'. השם קשור קשר הדוק לקדוש פרנסיס מאסיזי, שהיה איש דתי נודע במאה ה-13. השם משמש כסמל לשחרור ורוחניות.

in_greek.name: Φρανσίσκο
in_greek.meaning: Φρανσίσκο σημαίνει ελεύθερος άνθρωπος ή Γάλλος
in_greek.long_meaning: Φρανσίσκο είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από τα λατινικά, προερχόμενο από τη λέξη 'Φραγκίσκος', που σημαίνει 'ελεύθερος άνθρωπος' ή 'Γάλλος'. Το όνομα συνδέεται στενά με τον Άγιο Φραγκίσκο της Ασίζης, έναν εξέχοντα θρησκευτικό προσωπικό του 13ου αιώνα. Το όνομα χρησιμεύει ως σύμβολο απελευθέρωσης και πνευματικότητας.

in_latin.name: Franciscus
in_latin.meaning: Franciscus significat hominem liberum vel Francogallicum
in_latin.long_meaning: Franciscus est nomen Latinum, derivatum a voce 'Franciscus', quod significat 'hominem liberum' vel 'Francogallicum'. Nomen est arcte coniunctum cum Sancto Francisco Assisiensi, viri religiosi noti saeculi XIII. Nomen est symbolum liberationis et spiritualitatis.

historical_references.reference: Francisco de Borja, a Spanish nobleman and theologian, was born on October 15, 1510. He was the third son of the Duke of Gandía and a grandnephew of Pope Alexander VI. Borja entered the Society of Jesus in 1535 and was ordained a priest in 1538. He served as the first Superior General of the Society of Jesus from 1540 until his death in 1572.
historical_references.context: Counter-Reformation era, Church reform, Society of Jesus

historical_references.reference: Francisco de Miranda, a Venezuelan military leader, was born on February 1, 1750, in Caracas. He served in the Spanish army in America and Europe. In the late 18th century, he became a revolutionary leader in Venezuela, working for independence from Spain. He was exiled several times and died in France on February 14, 1816, at the age of 66.
